//: Cronsole Connect Pack v1.2 - MCP server wiring.
Newer copy: https://cronsole.mikesailab.com
Merge the `cronsole` entry below into your host's MCP config:
Claude Code  ->  .mcp.json in your project root, or ~/.claude.json
Claude Desktop -> claude_desktop_config.json
Cursor / Codex / others -> whatever file that host documents; the shape is the same.
Replace <PATH-TO-CRONSOLE> with where you installed Cronsole. The MCP server runs
dist/, not src/ - run `cd mcp-server && npm run build` once before first use, and
again after any update, or your change is invisible.
CRONSOLE_TOKEN is a ${ENV} reference on purpose so this file never holds the secret.
Export it in the environment you launch the host from. On Windows a newly set
variable needs a FRESH terminal - a process inherits its parent's environment, so
restarting the host inside an old terminal will not pick it up.
If CRONSOLE_TOKEN is unset, the literal text ${CRONSOLE_TOKEN} is forwarded and the API
answers 403 Invalid or expired token - which reads like an expired JWT and sends you
debugging auth instead of your environment. The server detects that and refuses to
start, so the tools go MISSING rather than erroring.
CRONSOLE_MCP_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE is omitted deliberately. Leaving it off keeps the
irreversible delete_task tool ABSENT from the tool list. The reversible verbs
(set_task_status, update_task_schedule, update_task_action) are always available -
prefer disabling a task over deleting it.
